english_translation: My parents were overjoyed when I told them that I had passed my final examinations.

dialogue.shona: Vabereki vangu vakafara zvikuru, pandakavaudza kuti ndapasa bvunzo dzangu dzekupedzisira.
dialogue.english: My parents were overjoyed when I told them that I had passed my final examinations.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Vabereki [people bereki] • vangu [people ngu] • vakafara [they (past) fara] • zvikuru [very much / greatly] • pandakavaudza [on / at ndakavaudza] • kuti [that / so that] • ndapasa [ndapasa] • bvunzo [bvunzo] • dzangu [dzangu] • dzekupedzisira [dzekupedzisira]

grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('vakafara')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'vakafara' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Connecting Clauses & Expressing Purpose with 'kuti'
grammar_notes.content: The connector 'kuti' is one of the most useful words in Shona. After verbs of speaking, thinking, or knowing (like 'akati' = said, 'unofunga' = you think, 'ndinoziva' = I know), 'kuti' means 'that'. However, when placed after an action verb, 'kuti' means 'so that / in order to', and the following verb changes its final vowel from '-a' to '-e'! For instance, '-dya' (eat) becomes 'kuti tidye' ('so that we may eat'), and '-wana' (get) becomes 'kuti uwane' ('so that you may get').
grammar_notes.rule: kuti + [Subject Prefix + Verb ending in -e] = 'so that [someone] may...' (e.g., kuti tidye = so that we eat)

grammar_notes.title: Possessive Pronouns: Saying 'My', 'Your', and 'Our' ('vangu')
grammar_notes.content: In Shona, possessive words like 'vangu' ('my/your/our/their') always follow the noun they belong to! The six core possessive stems are '-ngu' (my), '-ko' (your), '-ke' (his/her/its), '-du' (our), '-nyu' (your plural/polite), and '-vo' (their). A short linking sound ('wa-', 'ya-', 'ra-', 'cha-', 'dza-', 'ma-') attaches to the front of the stem to match the noun: for example, 'shamwari yangu' (my friend), 'munda wako' (your field), 'mabhuku edu' (our books), and 'kubudirira kwenyu' (your success).

cultural_notes.title: Family Celebrations When Examination Results ('Kupasa Bvunzo') Come Out
cultural_notes.content: When national O-Level, A-Level, or university final exam results are released in Zimbabwe, passing ('kupasa bvunzo dzekupedzisira') brings immense pride and ululation ('kupururudza') from parents ('vabereki') and extended family.

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new family sentence into English: 'Hanzvadzi yangu inoshanda muguta reHarare.'
options: My parents live at the rural homestead in Masvingo.
My friend passed all her school examinations this year.
The baby is sleeping quietly inside the bedroom.
My sibling works in the city of Harare.
active_exercises.correct_answer: My sibling works in the city of Harare.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Hanzvadzi yangu' = 'My sibling (brother/sister)', 'inoshanda' = 'works', 'muguta reHarare' = 'in the city of Harare'.

active_exercises.prompt: Complete this sentence using the Present Progressive ('is reading right now'): 'Shamwari yangu ______ bhuku idzva.'
active_exercises.explanation: 'Shamwari' uses the progressive form 'iri ku-' + '-verenga' (read) to mean 'is reading right now'.

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new sentence into English: 'Ndasiya nharembozha yangu pachigaro mumba yokutandarira.'
options: Please close the door and all the windows before sleeping.
I left my mobile phone on the chair in the living room.
My keys are inside the small bag on the table.
We are sitting under the shade tree outside the house.
active_exercises.correct_answer: I left my mobile phone on the chair in the living room.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Ndasiya' = 'I left', 'nharembozha yangu' = 'my mobile phone', 'pachigaro' = 'on the chair', 'mumba yokutandarira' = 'in the living room'.
